diagnostics.message:
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
google_bigquery_table.views creates BigQuery views whose `view.query` (from var.views) may read base tables created by google_bigquery_table.default in the same dataset. BigQuery validates/creates a view against the tables its query references, so the views must be created only after those tables exist. Currently google_bigquery_table.views depends only on google_bigquery_dataset.default (via dataset_id) and has no ordering edge to google_bigquery_table.default, so Terraform may create the views before the tables, causing "table not found" failures during apply. Add `depends_on = [google_bigquery_table.default]` to google_bigquery_table.views.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
google_bigquery_table.views defines views via an opaque `view.query` string that typically selects from the base tables created by google_bigquery_table.default. Terraform cannot infer this ordering from the SQL, so both resources may be created in parallel and BigQuery can reject the view with a "table not found" error because its referenced table does not yet exist. Add an explicit `depends_on = [google_bigquery_table.default]` to google_bigquery_table.views (there is no idiomatic attribute reference to wire in, since the query is user-supplied).

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
google_bigquery_table.views creates BigQuery views whose query strings (each.value.query) commonly reference tables created by google_bigquery_table.default in the same module. BigQuery resolves/validates a view's query against existing tables at creation time, so a view created before its underlying table exists fails with "Not found: Table". The dependency is not captured because the query is an opaque string with no attribute reference. google_bigquery_table.views should depend on google_bigquery_table.default (e.g. a bare depends_on = [google_bigquery_table.default]).
